title: [Epic] Bridges — vendor suites (DingTalk, WeCom, Feishu) behind the standard protocols the platform speaks: the platform's generic interfaces (webhook channel, inbound webhook, OIDC, SCIM) and the objectstack-ai/bridges repository
body:
repo:cloud#2 · os-zhuang · session_0123kRqqdpAJWYMgsgdAJX4G (filed on the maintainer's direction, handed off from the #27108 cloud-assessment thread)

Filing gate: ③ maintainer-directed, and ④ the cross-repo parent of its children. The maintainer, in the cloud project thread on 2026-10-28 (verbatim, not translated): 「钉钉这种不支持标准API的，有没有可能我们封装一层中转的微服务，按照标准协议」 (16:03Z) · 「用户映射、身份认证，这个属于单独的需求，能否也可以是另外一套中转服务」 (16:05Z) · 「我说的只是把钉钉作为例子，还会有企业微信，飞书等，你认为是中转服务的方式好，还是开发具体插件的方式好。」 (16:10Z, answered: bridges) · 「我创建了 bridges 仓库，你可以初始化，然后刚才讨论的问题立专题卡」 (16:15Z) · 「这个应该是单独的专题卡吧」 (16:16Z). And on the #27108 decision card 「插件专题 #27108 在中转方案之后怎么处理？」 the maintainer chose 「M1 做完，其余冻结」 (16:18Z). ⛔ Not a claim. ⛔ No `domain:*`: children span `objectstack` (server), `cloud` and `objectstack-ai/bridges`; triage sets each child's lane.

Dedupe: `bridge relay DingTalk WeCom Feishu webhook messaging channel OIDC SCIM` on objectstack → 0 hits (open or closed). Related, not duplicates: #27108 (code plugins), #27287 (SDK contract, frozen by this ruling), #27293 (zero-code connectors — this epic's action side reuses it).

## 维护者速读

钉钉、企业微信、飞书这类不讲标准协议的套件，不再做成代码插件，而是走独立的「中转服务」（bridge）：平台只讲标准协议，bridge 负责把标准协议翻译成厂商私有 API。平台补齐几个通用接口一次（出站 webhook 消息通道、入站 webhook、OIDC 登录、SCIM 通讯录），以后每接一家只是多一个 bridge，平台不改。bridge 放在新仓 `objectstack-ai/bridges`（公开、Apache-2.0，已初始化 `80b4abd`），每家一个包、各自发版；同一份代码既跑我们托管的多租户实例，也出 Docker 镜像给私有部署客户内网自部署。连带裁决：#27108 只做完 M1，M2–M5 与 SDK 冻结；托管 Cloud 不加载代码插件。

## Decisions this epic carries

| # | Decision | Effect |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | Vendor suites without a standard API (DingTalk, WeCom, Feishu, and the like) integrate through **bridges**, not code plugins. | #27108 ruling 6471792611 item 3 (`plugin-dingtalk` as the first resident of `objectstack-ai/plugins`) is withdrawn; DingTalk is this epic's first bridge. |
| 2 | **#27108: M1 finishes; M2, M3, M4, M5 and the SDK contract are frozen** until a paying customer asks for third-party code distribution. | #27124, #27125, #27284, #27285, #27287 frozen (recorded on #27108). M1 #27123 continues unchanged. |
| 3 | **Hosted ObjectOS Cloud loads no code plugins.** One hosted process serves many environments' kernels, so it is not a dedicated runtime (#27108 ruling item 4's rule, applied to hosted). Follows from decision 2 (no fetch or shelf path while M2/M4 are frozen); the thread's card on this question was closed as this option on that basis. | Code plugins are for self-hosted and Enterprise dedicated runtimes only (M1's local install). Hosted reaches vendor suites through bridges. |
| 4 | **Where the code lives.** Bridges: `objectstack-ai/bridges` (public, independent versions, no import of platform internals). Generic interfaces: `objectstack-ai/objectstack`. Our hosted bridge instances' deployment config: `objectstack-ai/cloud`, pinning a bridge release. | — |

## How a bridge meets the platform

| Need | Platform side (standard) | Bridge side |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Actions (send a work notice, create a to-do, read the directory) | OpenAPI / MCP connector app — #27293, no new card | calls the vendor API, reshapes requests and replies |
| Per-person notifications (approval → the approver's DingTalk) | **webhook messaging channel** — outbox exists, per-recipient channel missing (B1) | delivers to the person's vendor account |
| Callbacks (a button pressed in a vendor card) | **inbound webhook → flow** — exists (flow `api` trigger) | verifies and decrypts the vendor callback, forwards it |
| Sign-in (QR login, in-app silent login) | **OIDC** — exists both sides; hosted needs one upstream entry per bridge (B3) | wraps the vendor's OAuth / auth-code flow as an OIDC provider; no new "create a session from an external identity" API is needed |
| Directory and user mapping | **SCIM** provisioning into the environment — exists (cloud ADR-0071); gaps in B4 | reads the vendor directory; vendor user id → `externalId` (that IS the mapping; no mapping object) |

## Children (each filed by the owning lane, `Part of` this epic)

- **B1 — notification channel over the existing HTTP outbox** (objectstack, `server`, S). The delivery machinery exists: `plugin-webhooks` (`sys_webhook`, HMAC `X-Objectstack-Signature`, durable outbox, retries, cluster dispatcher; `packages/services/service-messaging/src/http-outbox.ts`) already POSTs **record events**. What is missing is a **per-recipient messaging channel**: `registerChannelProvider` is called for `email` and `sms` only (`messaging-service-plugin.ts:458`, `:477`), so a notification addressed to a person (recipient, preferences, template) cannot reach a URL. B1 = a `webhook` channel provider that enqueues into the same outbox, carrying the recipient's `externalId`, the rendered content and the deep link.
- **B2 — inbound callbacks: no card, already exists.** A flow's `api` start node arms a signed inbound hook (`packages/spec/src/automation/api-trigger-secret-ref.zod.ts`, `flow.zod.ts:1117`), and a wait node resumes on an incoming webhook (`node-executor.zod.ts:31`). The bridge verifies and decrypts the vendor callback, then posts to that hook.
- **B3 — "Sign in with <vendor>" on the Cloud identity center** (cloud, S). The mechanism exists on both sides: environments take an external OIDC/SAML IdP through `@better-auth/sso` (bring-your-own IdP; Business+ on hosted), and the Cloud identity center already federates social logins — but as a fixed list of Google / GitHub / Microsoft from environment variables (`packages/service-cloud/src/control-plane-preset.ts:444-450`). B3 = one generic OIDC upstream entry (better-auth `genericOAuth`) per bridge, so every hosted environment gets the button. Self-hosted: documentation only.
- **B4 — SCIM for bridges: two gaps only** (cloud + objectstack). SCIM itself is built: cloud ADR-0071 put `@better-auth/scim` (SCIM 2.0 `/Users`, `active:false` → ban + session revoke) in each environment, and the hosted kernel mounts it by plan (`planAllowsScim`, `packages/objectos-runtime/src/artifact-kernel-factory.ts:103`, `:315-355`; EE turns it on with the `FEATURE_SCIM` licence, `apps/objectos-ee/objectstack.config.ts:763-769`). A bridge is an external directory client, the same role as Okta, so ADR-0071 D2's "no cloud-as-SCIM-client" does not apply. What remains: (a) **Users only, no `/Groups`** (ADR-0071 D4): DingTalk departments → `sys_business_unit` and department → role are not covered — ADR-0071's out-of-scope line even names 钉钉 / 企业微信 / 飞书 org-structure sync; (b) **tier**: SCIM is Enterprise-only (cloud `docs/design/pricing.md:127`) — a maintainer decision (below) before a bridge relies on it for Team customers.
- **B5 — bridge-kit + bridge-dingtalk** (bridges). Kit: OIDC provider shell, SCIM client, webhook relay, vendor callback crypto (the token cache landed in `80b4abd`). DingTalk: actions (connector app's OpenAPI description), notifications (B1), sign-in (B3), directory (B4). Ships as our hosted instance and a Docker image. Acceptance carried over from #27287: an approval notification reaches a mapped DingTalk user with a deep link back to the record — plus sign-in with DingTalk and a directory sync.
- **B6 — compatibility** (bridges + objectstack). A nightly contract test of each bridge against the platform's `next` build, and a conformance kit for the standard interfaces in objectstack.
- WeCom and Feishu bridges are filed after DingTalk proves the kit.

## Open maintainer decisions (decision cards when the child is dispatched)

1. **Who registers the vendor app**: one ISV third-party app on the DingTalk open platform shared by all customers (better onboarding; needs ISV qualification and listing) vs each customer's own internal app with its key entered in the environment (works today).
2. **Tier**: is "Sign in with DingTalk" a social login (every tier, like Google/Microsoft), and is directory sync over SCIM Enterprise-only as SCIM is today — which would leave Team customers in China without it?

## Rules every child inherits

- ⛔ The platform never runs vendor code for this epic; a need that only in-process code can meet is a #27108 question, not a bridge.
- ⛔ Bridges are stateless toward customers: credentials arrive per request from the environment's own credential store and are never stored or logged; only derived tokens are cached (bridges `AGENTS.md`).
- ⛔ Bridges import no `@objectstack/*` internals; a missing standard interface is a platform card under this epic.

## Done-when

- B1 and B3 landed (and B4 for the gaps it carries), in the cloud pin.
- `bridge-dingtalk` released, hosted for ObjectOS Cloud and available as a Docker image; on a hosted environment a user signs in with DingTalk, the directory syncs, and an approval notification reaches the approver's DingTalk with a deep link.
- The nightly contract test runs green against platform `next`.

## Related

#27108 (code plugins; ruling recorded there) · #27287 (frozen) · #27293 (connector apps; cloud#3353 E4 shelf lists each bridge's connector app) · #27230 (credential S1) · ADR-0024 (identity) · `objectstack-ai/bridges` `docs/architecture.md`.
